evidence_excerpts: To achieve our goal, we design several domain-aware motion field adapters (\ie, MOFA-Adapters) to control the generated motions in the video generation pipeline. For MOFA-Adapters, we consider the temporal motion consistency of the video and generate the dense motion flow from the given sparse control conditions first, and then, the multi-scale features of the given image are wrapped as a guided feature for stable video diffusion generation.
requirements: The target video diffusion model must expose feature scales that can receive motion-guided residuals.
Sparse history evidence must be convertible into dense spatiotemporal guidance.
failure_boundaries: Motion-field guidance does not by itself estimate whether a correction improves a particular rollout.

evidence_excerpts: To tackle this, here we present the Video Motion Customization (VMC) framework, a novel one-shot tuning approach crafted to adapt temporal attention layers within video diffusion models. Our approach introduces a novel motion distillation objective using residual vectors between consecutive frames as a motion reference. The diffusion process then preserves low-frequency motion trajectories while mitigating high-frequency motion-unrelated noise in image space.
requirements: Temporal attention layers must be independently adaptable.
Consecutive-frame residuals must expose the motion component that should be preserved.
failure_boundaries: A one-shot motion objective can over-specialize and does not provide an execute-or-abstain benefit label.
2312.00845v1.extraction_rationale: The abstract binds temporal-attention adaptation to residual-vector motion distillation and frequency-separated trajectory preservation.

evidence_excerpts: To address these challenges, we introduce Ctrl-Adapter, an efficient and versatile framework that adds diverse controls to any image/video diffusion model through the adaptation of pretrained ControlNets. Ctrl-Adapter offers strong and diverse capabilities, including image and video control, sparse-frame video control, fine-grained patch-level multi-condition control (via an MoE router), zero-shot adaptation to unseen conditions
requirements: Source control features and target Ctrl-World features need an explicit alignment adapter.
The router must operate below whole-example granularity if correction benefit is spatially localized.
failure_boundaries: An MoE router over control conditions is not automatically calibrated to predictive benefit or abstention.
2404.09967v2.extraction_rationale: The abstract explicitly states cross-model control adaptation, sparse-frame video control, and patch-level multi-condition routing with an MoE.

evidence_excerpts: Understanding this process from a control system perspective shows that it forms a feedback-control system, where the control module receives a feedback signal from the generation process and sends a corrective signal back.

In this work, we take an existing controlling network (ControlNet) and change the communication between the controlling network and the generation process to be of high-frequency and with large-bandwidth. By doing so, we are able to considerably improve the quality of the generated images, as well as the fidelity of the control.
requirements: The frozen generator and corrector must exchange intermediate features at multiple depths or timesteps.
Corrective communication must not be delayed until a single terminal history-latent gain.
failure_boundaries: Dense feedback increases corrective bandwidth but can amplify harmful corrections without a selective benefit gate.
2312.06573v2.extraction_rationale: The abstract directly frames control as feedback and attributes gains to higher-frequency, higher-bandwidth corrective communication.

evidence_excerpts: We introduce a general-purpose conditioning method for neural networks called FiLM: Feature-wise Linear Modulation. FiLM layers influence neural network computation via a simple, feature-wise affine transformation based on conditioning information.

evidence_excerpts: we propose a novel meta-learning algorithm that learns to assign weights to training examples based on their gradient directions. To determine the example weights, our method performs a meta gradient descent step on the current mini-batch example weights (which are initialized from zero) to minimize the loss on a clean unbiased validation set.
requirements: A clean target-local validation frame must be isolated from the training minibatch.
The training system must support a bounded bilevel or first-order meta-gradient.
failure_boundaries: Validation-driven reweighting can overfit a tiny held-out context and must remain nested inside a separate promotion holdout.

evidence_excerpts: We present Residual Policy Learning (RPL): a simple method for improving nondifferentiable policies using model-free deep reinforcement learning. RPL thrives in complex robotic manipulation tasks where good but imperfect controllers are available. In these tasks, reinforcement learning from scratch remains data-inefficient or intractable, but learning a residual on top of the initial controller can yield substantial improvements.
requirements: A strong nominal predictor must remain available as the function-preserving base.
The residual objective must measure sequence-level improvement rather than only local reconstruction.
failure_boundaries: A fixed additive residual can degrade a strong nominal model when execution is not selective.
1812.06298v2.extraction_rationale: The abstract directly defines learning a residual on top of a strong but imperfect nominal controller.

evidence_excerpts: We give a new theoretical analysis and family of algorithms for predicting individual treatment effect (ITE) from observational data, under the assumption known as strong ignorability. The algorithms learn a "balanced" representation such that the induced treated and control distributions look similar.
requirements: Correction and no-correction examples must be paired or balanced well enough to estimate conditional benefit.
The treatment-effect estimate must be evaluated against unseen rollout contexts.
failure_boundaries: Strong ignorability does not automatically hold for adaptively generated world-model rollouts; randomized perturbation pairs are preferable.
1606.03976v5.extraction_rationale: The abstract explicitly defines individual treatment-effect prediction with a representation balancing treated and control distributions.

evidence_excerpts: Unlike prior methods that denoise future frames based on ground-truth context frames, Self Forcing conditions each frame's generation on previously self-generated outputs by performing autoregressive rollout with key-value (KV) caching during training. This strategy enables supervision through a holistic loss at the video level that directly evaluates the quality of the entire generated sequence, rather than relying solely on traditional frame-wise objectives. To ensure training efficiency, we employ a few-step diffusion model along with a stochastic gradient truncation strategy
requirements: Training must support generated-history rollouts and a sequence-level quality objective.
Gradient truncation must keep the rollout budget compatible with eight-card screening.
failure_boundaries: Self-forced full-model training can reintroduce backbone drift unless gradients are isolated to the new correction module.
2506.08009v2.extraction_rationale: The abstract explicitly binds generated-history training, holistic video-level supervision, rolling cache state, and truncated rollout gradients.
